authors: Zakšek, K., Oštir, K., Kokalj, Ž.
title: Sky-View Factor as a Relief Visualization Technique
one_line: Introduces sky-view factor, a diffuse-illumination relief visualization that shows small features without the directional bias of hillshade.

authors: Kokalj, Ž., Zakšek, K., Oštir, K.
title: Application of sky-view factor for the visualisation of historic landscape features in lidar-derived relief models
one_line: Shows on a Slovenian test site that sky-view factor reveals historic landscape features more clearly than single-source hillshade.

authors: Kokalj, Ž., Hesse, R.
title: Airborne laser scanning raster data visualization: A guide to good practice
venue: Prostor, kraj, čas 14 (ZRC SAZU, Založba ZRC)
one_line: Open-access practical guide to choosing and parameterising relief visualizations for archaeological interpretation of LiDAR DEMs.

authors: Kokalj, Ž., Somrak, M.
title: Why Not a Single Image? Combining Visualizations to Facilitate Fieldwork and On-Screen Mapping
one_line: Defines the VAT blend (visualization for archaeological topography), which combines several relief visualizations with blend modes into one image.

authors: Yokoyama, R., Shirasawa, M., Pike, R. J.
title: Visualizing Topography by Openness: A New Application of Image Processing to Digital Elevation Models
one_line: Introduces positive and negative topographic openness, an angular measure of how exposed or enclosed each DEM cell is.

authors: Doneus, M.
title: Openness as Visualization Technique for Interpretative Mapping of Airborne Lidar Derived Digital Terrain Models
one_line: Argues openness is free of directional bias and horizontal displacement, making it well suited to outlining archaeological features.

authors: Hesse, R.
title: LiDAR-derived Local Relief Models - a new tool for archaeological prospection
one_line: Introduces the local relief model, which removes large-scale landforms so small shallow features can be seen and measured.

authors: Štular, B., Kokalj, Ž., Oštir, K., Nuninger, L.
title: Visualization of lidar-derived relief models for detection of archaeological features
one_line: Systematically compares relief visualization techniques for detecting archaeological features in lidar DEMs.

authors: Bennett, R., Welham, K., Hill, R. A., Ford, A.
title: A Comparison of Visualization Techniques for Models Created from Airborne Laser Scanned Data
one_line: Quantitatively compares five techniques, from shaded relief to local relief and sky-view factor, against aerial-photo mapping of a UK study area.

authors: Devereux, B. J., Amable, G. S., Crow, P.
title: Visualisation of LiDAR terrain models for archaeological feature detection
one_line: Shows how hillshades lit from different directions can be combined into one image, the idea behind multidirectional hillshading for archaeology.

authors: Orengo, H. A., Petrie, C. A.
title: Multi-scale relief model (MSRM): a new algorithm for the visualization of subtle topographic change of variable size in digital elevation models
dataset: medium-resolution global DSMs (e.g. SRTM, ASTER GDEM, ALOS, TanDEM-X)
one_line: Multi-scale relief model that brings out subtle landforms of any size in global 30 m-class DSMs, used to map palaeochannels on an alluvial plain.

authors: Guyot, A., Hubert-Moy, L., Lorho, T.
title: Detecting Neolithic Burial Mounds from LiDAR-Derived Elevation Data Using a Multi-Scale Approach and Machine Learning Techniques

study_area.name: Carnac and Gulf of Morbihan, Brittany, France

one_line: Combines multi-scale topographic position with random forests to map megalithic burial mounds, finding a previously unknown mound at Carnac.

authors: Phong, B. T.
title: Illumination for computer generated pictures
one_line: The Phong reflection model (ambient, diffuse and specular terms) behind the app's Phong lighting mode.

authors: ZRC SAZU (EarthObservation)
title: Relief Visualization Toolbox in Python (RVT_py)
one_line: Open-source reference implementation of the RVT visualizations (hillshade, multidirectional hillshade, SVF, openness, LRM, VAT blends).

authors: Horn, B. K. P.
title: Hill shading and the reflectance map
one_line: Classic treatment of hill shading, including the 3x3 gradient estimator widely used for slope and aspect.

authors: Zevenbergen, L. W., Thorne, C. R.
title: Quantitative analysis of land surface topography
one_line: Fits a partial quartic surface to a 3x3 window to derive slope, aspect and profile and plan curvature.

authors: Florinsky, I. V.
title: Accuracy of local topographic variables derived from digital elevation models
venue: International Journal of Geographical Information Science 12
one_line: Analyses the errors of slope, aspect and curvature computed from gridded DEMs.

authors: Minár, J., Evans, I. S., Jenčo, M.
title: A comprehensive system of definitions of land surface (topographic) curvatures, with implications for their application in geoscience modelling and prediction
one_line: A systematic set of definitions for the many land-surface curvatures, with guidance on which to use.

authors: Guisan, A., Weiss, S. B., Weiss, A. D.
title: GLM versus CCA spatial modeling of plant species distribution
one_line: Early published use of the topographic position index (elevation relative to the neighbourhood mean) as a predictor.

authors: De Reu, J., Bourgeois, J., Bats, M., et al.
title: Application of the topographic position index to heterogeneous landscapes
one_line: Adapts TPI-based landform classification to landscapes of mixed relief.

authors: Wilson, J. P.
title: Digital terrain modeling
one_line: Review of digital terrain modelling and the land-surface parameters derived from DEMs.

authors: Hengl, T., Reuter, H. I. (eds.)
title: Geomorphometry: Concepts, Software, Applications
one_line: Standard reference book on land-surface parameters and objects extracted from DEMs.

authors: European Space Agency
title: Copernicus DEM - Global and European Digital Elevation Model
one_line: The Copernicus DEM (GLO-30 at 30 m worldwide), the surface model behind much of the app's global terrain.

authors: Farr, T. G., Rosen, P. A., Caro, E., et al.
title: The Shuttle Radar Topography Mission
one_line: Reference description of SRTM, the first near-global 1 to 3 arc-second DEM.

authors: Guth, P. L., Geoffroy, T. M.
title: LiDAR point cloud and ICESat-2 evaluation of 1 second global digital elevation models: Copernicus wins
dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, ALOS, ASTER, NASADEM, SRTM vs LiDAR and ICESat-2
one_line: Finds the Copernicus DEM consistently beats the other 1 arc-second global DEMs against LiDAR point clouds.

authors: Marešová, J., Gdulová, K., Pracná, P., et al.
title: Applicability of Data Acquisition Characteristics to the Identification of Local Artefacts in Global Digital Elevation Models: Comparison of the Copernicus and TanDEM-X DEMs
one_line: Evaluates the Copernicus DEM against the unedited TanDEM-X DEM in the Alps, Carpathians and Pyrenees, and how artefacts can be flagged.

authors: Bielski, C., López-Vázquez, C., Grohmann, C. H., et al.
title: Novel Approach for Ranking DEMs: Copernicus DEM Improves One Arc Second Open Global Topography
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 62
dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and other 1 arc-second global DEMs
one_line: Ranks open global DEMs with a multi-criteria method and confirms the Copernicus DEM as the best 1 arc-second option.

authors: Registry of Open Data on AWS
title: Copernicus Digital Elevation Model (DEM)
dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 / GLO-90 (Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF)
one_line: Public cloud-optimised copy of the Copernicus DEM on AWS.

authors: Registry of Open Data on AWS
title: Terrain Tiles
dataset: Mapzen/Tilezen terrain tiles (composite of global and national DEMs)
one_line: The Mapzen/Tilezen global Terrarium and GeoTIFF elevation tiles, one of the app's global sources.

authors: Mapterhorn
title: Mapterhorn
one_line: Open global terrain tileset used as the app's default elevation source.

authors: Inomata, T., Triadan, D., Vázquez López, V. A., et al.
title: Monumental architecture at Aguada Fénix and the rise of Maya civilization
one_line: Lidar reveals Aguada Fénix, the largest and oldest known monumental Maya platform.

authors: Inomata, T., Fernandez-Diaz, J. C., Triadan, D., et al.
title: Origins and spread of formal ceremonial complexes in the Olmec and Maya regions revealed by airborne lidar
one_line: Lidar over about 85,000 km2 of southern Mexico identifies 478 early ceremonial complexes sharing a common layout.

authors: Canuto, M. A., Estrada-Belli, F., Garrison, T. G., et al.
title: Ancient lowland Maya complexity as revealed by airborne laser scanning of northern Guatemala
one_line: Over 2,000 km2 of lidar across the Maya lowlands yields population estimates, agricultural works and defensive features.

authors: Chase, A. F., Chase, D. Z., Weishampel, J. F., et al.
title: Airborne LiDAR, archaeology, and the ancient Maya landscape at Caracol, Belize
one_line: Landmark lidar survey of the settlement, causeways and terraces of Caracol under rainforest canopy.

authors: Evans, D. H., Fletcher, R. J., Pottier, C., et al.
title: Uncovering archaeological landscapes at Angkor using lidar
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 110
one_line: Lidar reveals the forested urban grid and ceremonial centres of medieval Angkor.

authors: Doneus, M., Briese, C., Fera, M., Janner, M.
title: Archaeological prospection of forested areas using full-waveform airborne laser scanning
one_line: Shows full-waveform ALS can map an Iron Age hillfort and other earthworks under deciduous forest.

authors: Verschoof-van der Vaart, W. B., Lambers, K.
title: Learning to Look at LiDAR: The Use of R-CNN in the Automated Detection of Archaeological Objects in LiDAR Data from the Netherlands
venue: Journal of Computer Applications in Archaeology 2(1)
one_line: Deep-learning detection of barrows and Celtic fields in Dutch lidar, in an area with over 1,000 recorded barrows.

authors: Menze, B. H., Ur, J. A., Sherratt, A. G.
title: Detection of Ancient Settlement Mounds: Archaeological Survey Based on the SRTM Terrain Model
one_line: Uses the SRTM terrain model to detect and map tells (settlement mounds) across the Near East.

authors: Menze, B. H., Ur, J. A.
title: Mapping patterns of long-term settlement in Northern Mesopotamia at a large scale
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 109(14)
dataset: multispectral satellite time series plus a DEM (site volumes)
one_line: Maps about 14,000 settlement sites, tells included, over 23,000 km2 and uses DEM-derived mound volume as a proxy for how long a site was occupied.

authors: Orengo, H. A., Conesa, F. C., Garcia-Molsosa, A., et al.
title: Automated detection of archaeological mounds using machine-learning classification of multisensor and multitemporal satellite data
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 117(31)
dataset: Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral time series (no DEM)
one_line: Machine-learning classification of satellite imagery maps Indus-period mounded settlements in Cholistan, a non-DEM counterpart to relief-based mound detection.

authors: Crutchley, S., Crow, P.
title: Using Airborne Lidar in Archaeological Survey: The Light Fantastic
one_line: Historic England's guidance on deciding whether airborne lidar suits an archaeological project and how to process, visualise and interpret the data; it revises the 2010 English Heritage edition.

authors: Riley, S. J., DeGloria, S. D., Elliot, R.
title: A Terrain Ruggedness Index That Quantifies Topographic Heterogeneity
one_line: Defines the Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI), which measures the elevation difference between a cell and its eight neighbours.

authors: Weiss, A. D.
title: Topographic Position and Landforms Analysis
venue: Poster, ESRI User Conference, San Diego (The Nature Conservancy, Northwest Division)
one_line: Introduces landform classification from the Topographic Position Index (TPI) at two neighbourhood scales, giving ten classes from canyons to mountain tops.

authors: Sappington, J. M., Longshore, K. M., Thompson, D. B.
title: Quantifying Landscape Ruggedness for Animal Habitat Analysis: A Case Study Using Bighorn Sheep in the Mojave Desert
one_line: Defines the Vector Ruggedness Measure (VRM), which correlates less with slope than earlier indices, and shows that ruggedness and slope are separate parts of desert bighorn sheep habitat in three Mojave ranges.

authors: Hawker, L., Uhe, P., Paulo, L., et al.
title: A 30 m global map of elevation with forests and buildings removed
dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (corrected with machine learning: FABDEM)
one_line: Removes forests and buildings from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM with machine learning (FABDEM), lowering mean absolute error from 1.61 to 1.12 m in built-up areas and from 5.15 to 2.88 m in forests.

authors: Chase, A. F., Chase, D. Z., Fisher, C. T., et al.
title: Geospatial revolution and remote sensing LiDAR in Mesoamerican archaeology
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
one_line: Uses new lidar data from Caracol (Belize) and Angamuco (Mexico) to show how lidar maps whole ancient cities hidden under forest canopy.

authors: Evans, D.
title: Airborne laser scanning as a method for exploring long-term socio-ecological dynamics in Cambodia
one_line: Reports on airborne laser scanning at Angkor and elsewhere in Cambodia, including the 2015 campaign, which the paper calls the largest ever made for archaeology.

authors: Guyot, A., Lennon, M., Hubert-Moy, L.
title: Objective comparison of relief visualization techniques with deep CNN for archaeology
one_line: Benchmarks thirteen relief visualizations with a deep CNN that detects archaeological structures; e2MSTP, which builds on multiscale topographic position, performed best.

authors: Casana, J.
title: Radial route systems and agro-pastoral strategies in the Fertile Crescent: New discoveries from western Syria and southwestern Iran
dataset: not confirmed in this session (hollow-way mapping)
one_line: Reports newly found radial route systems (hollow ways) around sites in western Syria and southwestern Iran and discusses the agro-pastoral strategies they suggest.

authors: Johnson, K. M., Ouimet, W. B.
title: Rediscovering the lost archaeological landscape of southern New England using airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR)
one_line: Uses airborne lidar to rediscover relict historical land-use features hidden under the forests of southern New England.

authors: Trier, Ø. D., Cowley, D. C., Waldeland, A. U.
title: Using deep neural networks on airborne laser scanning data: Results from a case study of semi-automatic mapping of archaeological topography on Arran, Scotland
one_line: Tests whether a deep-learning detector developed in Norway transfers to Arran for roundhouses, shieling huts and clearance cairns; results range from usable to chaotic depending on the monument class.

authors: Clark, K. J., Nissen, E. K., Howarth, J. D., et al.
title: Highly variable coastal deformation in the 2016 MW7.8 Kaikōura earthquake reflects rupture complexity along a transpressional plate boundary

study_area.name: Kaikōura coast and Kaikōura Peninsula, New Zealand

one_line: Differences lidar from before and after the earthquake along about 110 km of coast and finds vertical displacements from -2.5 to +6.5 m, which require a revised multi-fault slip model.

authors: Haugerud, R. A., Harding, D. J., Johnson, S. Y., et al.
title: High-Resolution Lidar Topography of the Puget Lowland, Washington - A Bonanza for Earth Science
dataset: airborne lidar (Puget Sound Lidar Consortium), >10,000 km2
one_line: Leaf-off lidar of the forested Puget Lowland revealed previously unknown postglacial fault scarps, deep-seated landslides, uplifted beaches and glacial landforms.

authors: Chen, R.-F., Lin, C.-W., Chen, Y.-H., et al.
title: Detecting and Characterizing Active Thrust Fault and Deep-Seated Landslides in Dense Forest Areas of Southern Taiwan Using Airborne LiDAR DEM

study_area.name: Meilongshan Fault near Xinfa, Laolung River, Liugui District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan

one_line: Uses grayscale slope, openness with tinted slope and a red relief image map from 1 m lidar to confirm the Meilongshan Fault as an east-dipping thrust and to map a deep-seated landslide under dense forest.

authors: Scott, C. P., Arrowsmith, J. R., Nissen, E., et al.
title: The M7 2016 Kumamoto, Japan, Earthquake: 3-D Deformation Along the Fault and Within the Damage Zone Constrained From Differential Lidar Topography
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
dataset: pre- and post-event airborne lidar (differential topography)

study_area.name: Futagawa-Hinagu Fault Zone at Mashiki, Kumamoto, Kyushu, Japan

one_line: 3-D differencing of lidar from before and after the earthquake shows that only about 36% of horizontal and 62% of vertical deformation happened on the main fault trace; the rest was spread through the damage zone.

authors: Shugar, D. H., Jacquemart, M., Shean, D., et al.
title: A massive rock and ice avalanche caused the 2021 disaster at Chamoli, Indian Himalaya
dataset: satellite imagery and DEMs (data details not checked in this session)

study_area.name: Ronti Peak north face and Ronti Gad, Chamoli, Uttarakhand, India

one_line: Traces the February 2021 disaster to a rock and glacier-ice collapse from Ronti Peak that turned into a highly mobile debris flow and struck hydropower plants downstream.

authors: Dietterich, H. R., Diefenbach, A. K., Soule, S. A., et al.
title: Lava effusion rate evolution and erupted volume during the 2018 Kīlauea lower East Rift Zone eruption
dataset: repeat DEMs from small UAS, airborne lidar and airborne InSAR, plus bathymetry

study_area.name: Kīlauea lower East Rift Zone, Hawaii

one_line: Repeat topography during the eruption gives 0.9-1.4 km3 of lava (dense-rock equivalent), 0.4 km3 of it on land, with effusion rates rising to 200 m3/s or more by mid-June.

authors: Aufaristama, M., Höskuldsson, Á., Ulfarsson, M. O., et al.
title: Lava Flow Roughness on the 2014-2015 Lava Flow-Field at Holuhraun, Iceland, Derived from Airborne LiDAR and Photogrammetry
one_line: Uses the Topographic Position Index and the Hurst exponent to characterise the roughness of spiny lava, a lava pond, blocky surfaces and an inflated channel.

authors: Pedersen, G. B. M., Belart, J. M. C., Óskarsson, B. V., et al.
title: Volume, Effusion Rate, and Lava Transport During the 2021 Fagradalsfjall Eruption: Results From Near Real-Time Photogrammetric Monitoring
one_line: Near-real-time DEM differencing over the six-month eruption gives a 4.8 km2 lava field with a bulk volume of 150 +/- 3 million m3 and a mean thickness over 30 m.

authors: Mannerfelt, E. S., Dehecq, A., Hugonnet, R., et al.
title: Halving of Swiss glacier volume since 1931 observed from terrestrial image photogrammetry
dataset: historical DEMs from terrestrial photographs (1916-1947) differenced with modern DEMs
one_line: Builds DEMs from about 21,700 archived terrestrial photographs (median date 1931) and differences them with modern DEMs, finding that Swiss glacier volume halved between 1931 and 2016.

authors: Yu, P., Eyles, N., Sookhan, S.
title: Automated drumlin shape and volume estimation using high resolution LiDAR imagery (Curvature Based Relief Separation): A test from the Wadena Drumlin Field, Minnesota
one_line: Separates drumlins from the regional surface with a curvature-based method on lidar and estimates the shape and volume of each drumlin automatically.

authors: Jones, B. M., Grosse, G., Arp, C. D., et al.
title: Recent Arctic tundra fire initiates widespread thermokarst development

study_area.name: Anaktuvuk River tundra fire scar, North Slope, Alaska

one_line: Differencing lidar DTMs from two and seven years after the 2007 fire detects thaw subsidence across 34% of the burned tundra, compared with less than 1% in similar unburned terrain.

authors: Zhu, J., Taylor, T. P., Currens, J. C., et al.
title: Improved Karst Sinkhole Mapping in Kentucky Using Lidar Techniques: A Pilot Study in Floyds Fork Watershed
venue: Journal of Cave and Karst Studies

study_area.name: Floyds Fork watershed, Jefferson County, Kentucky, USA

one_line: Extracting closed depressions from a lidar DEM found 1,683 probable sinkholes where 383 had been mapped; field checks confirmed 106 of 121.

authors: Stefanovski, S., Kokalj, Ž., Stepišnik, U.
title: Sky-view factor enhanced doline delineation: A comparative methodological review based on case studies in Slovenia
one_line: Delineates dolines by combining hydrological tools with the sky-view factor on a 1 m DEM and compares the result with depression filling (fit for identification only) and U-Net segmentation.

authors: de Matos-Machado, R., Toumazet, J.-P., Bergès, J.-C., et al.
title: War landform mapping and classification on the Verdun battlefield (France) using airborne LiDAR and multivariate analysis
dataset: airborne LiDAR DTM of the whole battlefield
one_line: Self-organising maps and clustering of lidar morphometry map more than a million First World War landforms (shell craters, shelters, gun positions) in eight shape classes; 93% of shell craters were correctly classified.

authors: Gheyle, W., Stichelbaut, B., Saey, T., et al.
title: Scratching the surface of war. Airborne laser scans of the Great War conflict landscape in Flanders (Belgium)

study_area.name: Former Ypres front zone, West Flanders, Belgium

one_line: The Flanders lidar DTM reveals previously unknown Great War remains (trenches, dugouts, shelled ground) in the former front zone, using sky-view factor and relief-model visualizations.

authors: Magnini, L., Bettineschi, C., De Guio, A.
title: Object-based Shell Craters Classification from LiDAR-derived Sky-view Factor
one_line: Counts the remaining First World War shell craters on an Alpine plateau by object-based classification of a lidar sky-view factor image.

authors: Suh, J. W., Anderson, E., Ouimet, W., et al.
title: Mapping Relict Charcoal Hearths in New England Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks and LiDAR Data
one_line: A U-Net fed with slope, hillshade and VAT rasters detects relict charcoal hearths, with F1 up to 95.5% in small test regions and 86% over a 493 km2 town.

authors: Raab, A., Bonhage, A., Schneider, A., et al.
title: Spatial distribution of relict charcoal hearths in the former royal forest district Tauer (SE Brandenburg, Germany)

study_area.name: Tauer forest district near Peitz, Spree-Neisse, Brandenburg, Germany

one_line: About 6,000 relict charcoal hearths were digitised from shaded-relief maps over 109 km2 of former royal forest that fuelled the Peitz ironworks (16th-19th century).

authors: Laporte-Fauret, Q., Castelle, B., Marieu, V., et al.
title: Coastal Dune Morphology Evolution Combining Lidar and UAV Surveys, Truc Vert beach 2011-2019
dataset: airborne lidar and UAV photogrammetry, plus historical aerial photographs

study_area.name: Le Truc Vert, Lège-Cap-Ferret, Gironde, France

one_line: Combines historical aerial photographs, airborne lidar and UAV surveys to track how the coastal dune at Truc Vert changed between 2011 and 2019.

authors: Fink, C. M., Drohan, P. J.
title: High Resolution Hydric Soil Mapping using LiDAR Digital Terrain Modeling
venue: Soil Science Society of America Journal
one_line: A logistic regression on 1 m lidar slope and 5 m lidar depressions predicts hydric soils better than the 10 m USGS DEM.

authors: Trevisani, S., Skrypitsyna, T. N., Florinsky, I. V.
title: Global digital elevation models for terrain morphology analysis in mountain environments: insights on Copernicus GLO-30 and ALOS AW3D30 for a large Alpine area
dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and ALOS AW3D30 against an airborne lidar reference DEM
one_line: Across 6,210 km2 of Trentino, GLO-30 beats AW3D30 on gentle, unvegetated and urban terrain, AW3D30 does slightly better on rough, steep terrain, and neither captures fine-scale morphology on steep slopes.

authors: Kooistra, M. J., Maas, G. J.
title: The widespread occurrence of Celtic field systems in the central part of the Netherlands

study_area.name: Central Netherlands just north of the Rhine

one_line: AHN laser altimetry detected about 1,200 ha of Iron Age Celtic field systems, about 1,050 ha of them new, and suggests about 4,500 ha originally.

authors: Prümers, H., Betancourt, C. J., Iriarte, J., et al.
title: Lidar reveals pre-Hispanic low-density urbanism in the Bolivian Amazon
dataset: airborne lidar (with TanDEM-X 12 m for context)

study_area.name: Casarabe culture sites, Llanos de Mojos, Beni, Bolivia

one_line: Lidar reveals two large Casarabe-culture settlements, Cotoca (147 ha) and Landívar (315 ha), with platforms, ramparts, causeways and canals in a four-tier settlement system.

authors: Khan, S., Bartley, R., Kinsey-Henderson, A., et al.
title: Assessing gully erosion and rehabilitation using multi temporal LiDAR DEMs: Case study from the Great Barrier Reef catchments, Australia
venue: International Soil and Water Conservation Research
dataset: multi-temporal airborne LiDAR DEMs 0.5 m (DEMs of Difference)

study_area.name: Bowen-Bogie catchment, Burdekin Basin, Queensland, Australia

one_line: Repeat 0.5 m lidar at three gullies gives untreated erosion rates of 14-53 t/ha/yr and shows that rehabilitation raises the share of fine sediment kept in the gully to about 60%.
